relatedSnapshot.title: Charged twice for the same domain and inbox bundle; one bundle was never delivered and its subscription is still billing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: customer-initiated Intercom conversation, opened 2026-09-30, contact Name 6 <email>, workspace "Name 7 Workspace", owner role. Initial message: "I have a billing issue that isn't being sorted. Please escalate to someone asap!" Asked for detail: "I've been billed twice for emails and domains for the last 3 months when that's not what I'm using." Declined the self-serve answer: "No, I still need help." No attachments.

Bucket: overcharged.

Finding: the customer bought the same DFY bundle (1 domain + 3 inboxes) twice about 17 hours apart and was charged for both; only one bundle was ever delivered. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-23 14:01Z) was cancelled for "Payment timeout - order automatically cancelled after 30 minutes" with nothing provisioned, but its Autumn subscription and its Stripe charges landed anyway. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-24 06:47Z) completed and is the bundle the customer actually uses (3 active connected inboxes). The cancelled order's subscription was never cancelled, so it has kept invoicing every month since.

Exposure (Stripe, smallest currency unit, all succeeded and unrefunded, no credit notes):

* 2026-07-23, 3276 cents ($32.76), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0017
* 2026-08-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0021
* 2026-09-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0025
  Total already collected for the undelivered bundle: $68.76, and $18.00/month continues until the orphan subscription is cancelled. The delivered bundle's own charges are legitimate and are not part of this ask.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise): refund the $68.76 collected for the undelivered bundle, and cancel the orphan domain and inbox line items on the billing account so the recurring $18.00/month stops. A Stripe customer credit is the alternative if the customer would rather have it applied forward (the Legacy Pro plan bills monthly, so there is a future invoice to consume it). The customer has not yet said which they want. No money has been moved and nothing has been cancelled.

Full readout, systems of record, and the code path are in the Billing investigation document on this ticket.

relatedSnapshot.title: Overcharged for inbox and domain seats — billed 24 inbox seats while 12 live on the workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: customer-initiated Intercom conversation. Contact Name 11, <email>, workspace "Company Four" (the billing URL in the conversation pins it: <url:app.acquisity.ai>). She opened with "i have a billing question", attached a screenshot of the Billing page and asked "why does my billing say i owe $96/month for 12 total inboxes but then it says below $24/month x 4 domains," then "then why am i getting billed double that per month", then "speak to a human". Fin AI twice explained it away as the same cost shown two ways; she did not accept that. She then sent a second screenshot of the page's "Invoices & payment history" table and asked "checking the Payment history, there were other charges. Where is this coming from?" No requested remedy stated, only that the monthly amount looks wrong.

Bucket: overcharged.

Finding: the Billing page is not double counting. The $96/month "Total Inboxes" line and the "$24/month x 4 domains" rows are the same 12 inboxes recomputed, which is why they agree. The real divergence is that her billing account carries 24 inbox seats and 8 domain seats while the workspace holds 12 live inboxes on 4 active domains.

* Billed: 18 inbox seats ($24 + $24 + $96 = $144.00/month) + 6 inbox seats (6 x $8.00 = $48.00/month) = $192.00/month; and 6 + 2 = 8 domain seats = $144.00/year; plus a $1.00/month legacy plan.
* Live: 4 active domains with 3 prewarmed inboxes each = 12 inboxes.
* Excess: 12 inbox seats ($96.00/month) and 4 domain seats ($72.00/year). The excess inbox seats are exactly the $96/month she pointed at.

Her second screenshot answers "where is this coming from". Every row is a real paid invoice on this billing account, and the two recurring lines are the two subscriptions renewing on different days of the month: $144.00 on the 24th (the 18-seat subscription) and $48.00 on the 19th (the older 6-seat legacy subscription). The $23.75 and $10.00 rows are one-off credit purchases, not subscriptions, so they are not part of the recurring cost. Nothing in the history is a duplicate, a refund, a credit note, or a failed payment.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise): reconcile the live add-on seats on the billing account against the resources genuinely in the workspace, end the excess inbox and domain line items so the recurring charge stops, and decide the refund of the overcollected amount against the uncapped charge history. She has no self-serve path to remove the excess seats.

Open human decisions: the customer has not yet said whether she wants money back or a credit, and the suspended <domain> domain's 3 inboxes are excluded from the Billing page but not obviously excluded from billing.

relatedSnapshot.title: DFY domain orders that fail leave names claimed and un-cancellable, blocking re-purchase and leaving the domain store inconsistent
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Root cause

When a Done-For-You domain order fails to provision at the provider, the domain rows are written to `mail_domain` (which has a global unique index `mail_domain_domain_unique` on `domain`) and left in a `failed` or `pending` state. Those rows are never released, so they keep holding the name for the original organization. A later order for the same name throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization" at the claim step, silently drops the overlapping domains, and leaves the new order stuck in `provisioning`.

Separately, a domain that failed still renders in Billing with no Cancel option, and the domain store availability check reads the registrar/provider (which never registered the failed name) instead of `mail_domain`. The result is a failed domain that shows as "available to purchase" while its name is actually still claimed internally.

## Evidence

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts` `processCreateColdMailOrder`: claims domains into `mail_domain` (unique on `domain`), throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization: ..." when a name is already held, and on provider failure writes domains to `status='failed'` with the order left `requires_attention` or `provisioning`.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`: retries failed inboxes on `requires_attention` orders, but does not release a domain name that failed at the provider and does not recover the duplicate-domain-claim collision.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-08-27)

Domain orders stuck in a non-terminal provisioning state: 17 `provisioning` across 17 organizations, 66 `requires_attention` across 66 organizations, 17 `failed` across 16 organizations. Done-For-You specifically: 3 `provisioning`, 26 `requires_attention`.

Domains in `failed` status with at least one `active` inbox (counted 2026-09-05): 106 domains across 41 organizations.

Paid `requires_attention` orders older than 7 days that hold `failed` domains (counted 2026-09-11): 26 orders across 25 organizations, holding 51 failed domains. Never-retried `error` inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days: 33, across 5 organizations. A 2026-09-10 count of the same cohort returned identical figures.

DFY orders stranded by a stale cross-organization `mail_domain` claim, with no saved provider order id and stale beyond 24 hours (counted 2026-09-23): 5 orders across 5 organizations and 5 users, from the ENG-14139 report. Collision cascade as of 2026-09-23: one stale failed claim is a foreign claim on 4 later DFY orders across 4 organizations, and pending claims written by two stuck orders block 4 further organizations' orders. The wider stuck-in-`provisioning` population is 9 orders across 9 organizations, of which 4 belong to ENG-13308's stall mechanism.

## Fix direction

* Release a failed domain's claim so the name can be re-purchased, and reconcile the domain store's availability check against owned-but-failed domains.
* Stop silently dropping overlapping domains from a new DFY order; fail fast with a clear message to the customer instead.
